title: The Psalm Every Anxious Person Should Read
paragraphs:
The Psalm Every Anxious Person Should Read
When Your Mind Won’t Stop Running, Your Heart Won’t Stop Breaking, and Fear Feels Stronger Than Faith
Not because people do not care.
But because some wars happen in complete silence.
You smile while your thoughts are collapsing.
You answer messages while your chest feels heavy.
You sit in church, sing the songs, nod through the sermon, and still go home carrying a storm nobody knows exists.
Then pick the burden back up before the day ends.
And somewhere in the middle of all of it, you begin asking questions you never thought you would ask.
"Why can't I stop feeling this way?"
"Why does my mind keep returning to the same fears?"
"Why am I exhausted even when nothing happened today?"
If that sounds familiar, there is a Psalm you need to read.

Because thousands of years before psychologists gave names to anxiety, before social media amplified comparison, before endless notifications trained our minds to live in constant alertness, a shepherd named David sat alone with fears that felt larger than himself.
And under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, he wrote words that still reach anxious hearts today.
Because Psalm 23 is not merely a funeral passage.
It is a lifeline for weary souls.
David begins with words that are far more radical than many realize:
"The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1)
"The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing."
David is not saying he possesses everything he desires.
He is declaring that because God Himself is his Shepherd, he possesses everything he truly needs.
Anxiety often grows from the fear that we will not have enough.
Yet David begins by declaring that the Shepherd Himself is enough.
But because God's presence is greater than the uncertainty surrounding him.
The Shepherd is not merely guiding the sheep.
The Shepherd becomes the sheep's security.
"He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul."
Notice what David does not say.
Because anxiety often feels like losing pieces of yourself.
But God specializes in restoring fragmented souls.
The God who created you knows how to rebuild what fear has damaged.
And then comes the verse every anxious person eventually needs.
Not because it removes the valley.
But because it changes who walks through it with you.
"Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me."
Psalm 23 never promises a valley-free life.
Christianity has never been the promise of a painless existence.
"In the world you will have tribulation." (John 16:33)
"Take heart; I have overcome the world."
The presence of Christ inside them.
But in the valley he suddenly talks to God.
Fear often transforms theology into intimacy.
What was once information becomes relationship.
What was once doctrine becomes dependence.
What was once knowledge becomes survival.
Many people discover God's closeness only after reaching the place they hoped never to visit.
And perhaps that is where you are right now.
You may not understand the valley.
But Psalm 23 reminds us that the Shepherd never abandons His sheep there.
The greatest comfort is not finding answers.
The greatest comfort is finding Him.
That truth reaches its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
The One Psalm 23 was ultimately pointing toward.
The One who leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one.
The One who walks into darkness to rescue the lost.
The One who carries broken sheep instead of condemning them.
The One who took our sin upon Himself at the cross.
The One who entered death and emerged victorious through the resurrection.
The scandal of the Gospel is that humanity rebelled against God.
The grace of the Gospel is that God pursued humanity anyway.
That is the story of Scripture.
That is the story of Psalm 23.
That is the story of Jesus.
And perhaps that is your story too.
The enemy wants you trapped in fear.
Jesus wants you transformed by faith.
Not because your circumstances instantly change.
But because your Shepherd remains faithful even when circumstances do not.
Maybe today you feel like your life has become a scandal.
A collection of failures, regrets, fears, and wounds.
But the Gospel has always been about God rewriting stories.
The cross itself became the greatest example.
What looked like history's greatest defeat became humanity's greatest victory.
So before you close this article, stop for a moment.
But because your Shepherd remains present.
Let every word remind you that your anxiety is not your identity.
Your fear is not your master.
Your valley is not your destination.
And if this message spoke to your heart, do not keep it to yourself.
What part of Psalm 23 do you need most right now?
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
Because sometimes the article you share becomes the answer to someone else's prayer.
